On Wed, May 26, 2027 at 09:27, Chloe Martin wrote:
> Team — forwarding Optima's report. Quick read below.

Initial triage notes (observed 08:40–09:20 ET):
- No scheduled model rollouts in the last 48 hours. Model hash stable on hosted catalog.
- Spike correlates with an increase in fallback to a smaller/quantized model variant for mixed workloads. Fallback rate jumped from ~2% to ~38% at 08:45.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 96% to 61% at the same window (likely cache invalidation from cross-customer prefix change).
- Several worker hosts in us-east-1 reported transient OOMs leading to request retries; autoscaler added capacity but warm-up plus cold KV caches amplified latency.

Attaching: kvcache_miss_snapshot.json (sample), worker-oom-log-08-45.txt (excerpt).

Short actions I recommend now:
1) Temporarily pin Optima's route to the stable model variant (disable automatic fallback) — reduces quality risk but will lower error rate and latency.
2) Force warm-up of new hosts' model weights and populate KV cache with hot prefixes (fast prefill job).
3) Increase aggressive retry budget and route non-critical traffic to lower-tier pool until warm caches are ready.

I'll start the pin and warm-up now; will report back in 20 minutes with metrics.

—Monica
SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid response team. A few items for the customer comms and exec timeline:

Customer-facing talking points (short):
- What happened: transient cache invalidation + autoscaler warm-up coupled with higher-than-expected fallback to quantized variant caused elevated latency and error rate.
- Immediate impact: sustained p95/p99 degradation and ~5–7% error rate affecting recommendation flows.
- What we are doing: pinned to stable model variant, warm-up/fill KV caches, prioritized traffic, and monitoring to confirm recovery.
- ETA: visible improvement expected within 30–90 minutes post warm-up; full regression verification in 4 hours.
- Next steps: daily incident brief for 3 days; formal RCA in 72 hours.

Please use the draft customer note in the attached customer_comm_draft_0526.md and send after Monica confirms p95/p99 trending back down. I'll prepare an internal exec note for Optima leadership once we have a stabilization signal.

Tom/Sarah — follow-up after overnight monitoring and stabilization efforts. Thank you for your patience and for working with our oncall. Summary below:

- The pin to the stable variant and targeted warm-up executed at 09:55 ET on 5/26. Warm prefill completed by 10:25 ET.
- p95 reduced from 1.4s (peak) to ~260ms within ~35 minutes of the warm-up; p99 back to ~480ms. Error rate dropped below 0.7% and throughput returned to baseline by 13:10 ET.

Actions taken:
- Permanent change: disabled automatic cross-model fallback for Optima's production route pending RCA.
- Hot-prefix prefill is now part of our regional warm-up playbook (playbook attached).
- We will run a full RCA (timeline: 72 hours) and provide the technical appendix and remediation plan.

Customer remediation:
- We will issue SLA credit for the affected window as discussed; Aditya will follow up with paperwork.
- We've enabled a temporary reserved capacity buffer for the next 48 hours and increased monitoring thresholds on Optima's route.

Next touchpoints:
- Tactical sync today 10:30 ET (30 min) — invite sent.
- Daily incident brief at 17:00 ET for next 3 days unless cancelled.

Attachments: incident_playbook_v2.pdf, customer_comm_draft_0526.md
